title: BART heavy-rail service, ridership and operating cost
question: How did passenger trips, railcar service hours and reported operating expenses change across the pandemic?
finding: Heavy rail carried 125.1 million unlinked trips in FY2019, 17.1 million in FY2021 and 56.6 million in FY2025. FY2025 railcar revenue hours were 2.17 million versus 2.23 million in FY2019. Reported operating expenses increased from $651.0 million to $885.6 million over those six years.
how: The Federal Transit Administration’s TS2.1 series supplies annual reported operating expenses, passenger trips, vehicle revenue miles and vehicle revenue hours. Filtered to BART agency 90003, directly operated heavy rail. Passenger trips and dollars per railcar revenue hour use the same mode, year and denominator.
limits: Railcar revenue hours differ from train operating hours, and unlinked boardings can count a transferring passenger twice. The figures exclude BART’s hybrid rail, people mover, buses and paratransit. Pandemic and remote-work changes reduced demand. Train lengths, frequency and service patterns affect railcar hours. Dollars are nominal and do not isolate inflation or avoidable expense.
